entries.91ce6259c4c380d9: A fabless semiconductor vendor that develops and supplies dedicated SoCs for each customer in the logic semiconductor market. To take advantage of the benefits of a semiconductor industry with growing horizontal specialization, it owns no factories and outsources product manufacturing to [[term:foundry|foundry]] companies, led by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited (TSMC), and to specialist providers such as OSAT, which offer contract [[term:back-end-process|back-end process]] manufacturing services. Money comes in through two stages: during the design and development stage, it receives most of the cost of design and development from customers in stages as NRE revenue, and during the mass production stage, it receives product revenue, which accounts for the majority of total revenue. Because it usually takes more than two years from winning a deal until design and development and customer evaluation are complete and mass production begins, the company states that, as a company responsible for developing and supplying customers’ core components over a long period, it operates on a solid financial foundation.
entries.c05cd5832771939d: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥12,354 million (down 50.6% year on year), ordinary profit was ¥11,756 million (down 53.2%), and net income attributable to owners of the parent was ¥8,733 million (down 55.4%). The company explains that this was due to mass production of new products with comparatively low gross margins starting, which raised the product cost ratio, and to development investment for advance development continuing at a high level.
entries.d7c7ec5aca32c8b4: This is revenue received in the mass production stage. It accounts for the large majority of total revenue. In the fiscal year ended March 2026 it was ¥161,792 million (up 10.4% year on year); the company explains that although demand for communication equipment in the Chinese market declined, sales of new in-vehicle mass-production products in China and some industrial products began to increase from the second quarter onward.
entries.dbd1261b9552e201: Socionext's business is a single [[term:segment|segment]] centered on SoCs developed under its 'Solution SoC' business model. ＳｏＣ (System on Chip) is a [[term:semiconductor|semiconductor]] chip that implements some or all of the functions required for the operation of a device or system in one chip. In conventional ASICs, upstream design such as architecture design, planning, specification design and logic design is performed by the customer itself; the feature of 'Solution SoC' is that Socionext performs this upstream design together with the customer. Its focus areas are automotive, data center/networking, smart devices and industrial, to which the ＩｏＴ＆radar sensing field, including radio-wave ranging sensors, is added. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥200,834 million.
entries.de4121c628e1bd44: The company works with customers to define specifications and perform logical design, combining advanced technologies provided by external vendors to design and develop the SoC best suited to each customer. The company cites its strengths as design and development capability spanning software through subsystems, and its overall capability covering mass production, quality assurance and SCM. It characterizes the Solution SoC as avoiding vendor lock-in because it is not based on the company's own ASSP.
entries.e3046dacec174a92: Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥200,834 million, up 6.5% from the previous year. The breakdown is product sales of ¥161,792 million, NRE revenue of ¥38,325 million and other revenue of ¥717 million. Annual business negotiation wins (converted at US$1 = ¥120) were approximately ¥310 billion, below approximately ¥360 billion in the previous year, but the company explains that it won large deals centered on the data center and network fields.

entries.fe192edd86084543: This is revenue received from customers in the design and development stage before mass production (ＮＲＥ = Non-Recurring Engineering). It corresponds to development-stage costs such as personnel costs, IP, design tools, reticles and prototype manufacturing, and is usually recorded in several installments according to development progress. In the fiscal year ended March 2026 it was ¥38,325 million (down 6.6% year on year). The share of ＮＲＥ revenue accounted for by projects using advanced process nodes of 7nm or finer was 84% in the fiscal year ended March 2026.
